summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory (mode 1777, owner root:root) using the sticky bit so any user can create files but only the file owner (or root) can delete/rename them. Verified functionally with two test users pre- and post-reboot, then restarted node1 and confirmed the configuration persisted with a changed boot identity.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop via sudo mkdir, set owner root:root, mode 1777 (sticky bit)
Verified sticky-bit semantics: created dropuser1/dropuser2, confirmed each could write their own file but not delete the other's file (rm -> Operation not permitted)
Cleaned up test files and test users, confirmed /srv/drop left empty with 1777 root:root
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, and /srv/drop permissions/mount (on persistent root filesystem, not tmpfs)
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1 in background so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again (first poll got connection refused, second succeeded)
Confirmed boot_id changed (f41e1f8a... -> 1d269819...) proving an actual restart, and /srv/drop retained 1777 root:root
Re-ran the two-user write/delete test post-reboot to confirm sticky-bit protection survived the restart, then cleaned up test users/files

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with sticky bit (users cannot delete others' files)
evidence.summary: Directory created with mode 1777 root:root; two test users each wrote their own file, and cross-user rm attempts failed with 'Operation not permitted', while same-owner writes succeeded.

evidence.requirement: Cleanup left /srv/drop in final clean state
evidence.summary: Test files removed and test users deleted; /srv/drop shown empty with correct 1777 root:root permissions.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline for node1 (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f41e1f8a-dd2a-4b61-aa04-d64b0923b603 and uptime, plus confirmed /srv/drop (1777 root:root) resides on the persistent root filesystem /dev/vda1, not tmpfs.
systemctl reboot issued in background via nohup; command returned immediately with PID before the node dropped.

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable then reachable again after restart
evidence.summary: First poll got SSH connection refused (node down/rebooting); second poll succeeded, confirming node1 came back online.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 1d269819-6cfc-45de-9d09-97f937972bae, different from the pre-restart f41e1f8a-... value, and uptime -s shows a new boot time.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and sticky-bit behavior
evidence.summary: /srv/drop still shows 1777 root:root after reboot; functional re-test with two fresh users confirmed writes succeed and cross-user deletes are still blocked with 'Operation not permitted', then test artifacts were cleaned up leaving /srv/drop empty.
